name: CPU temperature, fan and power
plain: No API reads CPU heat; only coarse pressure buckets exist.
meaning: Compute Pressure API (Chrome 125, secure context) returns nominal, fair, serious or critical, throttled to at most 1 update per second and capped per origin. Exact degrees, fan speed and wattage are not exposed. Battery level is separate.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: rate limit
fields.range: default sample interval 1000 ms, min 1 s

limits.headline: Can't see your CPU heat, fan speed, or power use
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: Check four coarse busy levels in Chrome and Edge (nominal to critical)
Get an update at most once a second
Slow down heavy work when the level gets high
cannot: See degrees, fan speed, or watts
Check busy levels in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
Check it from a hidden tab or a page that is not HTTPS
Check it if the site or iframe is blocked by Permissions Policy
limits.differs: Only Chrome and Edge offer the coarse levels. Firefox and Safari offer none.

story.what_it_is: No tool lets a page read how hot your processor is. Only coarse busy levels exist.

marketing.name: Compute Pressure API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a coarse busy signal instead of raw temperature readings.

story.for_you: A site cannot see your laptop's temperature or fan speed. The nearest thing is a basic busy level, so a video call can lower quality before your laptop overheats.
story.for_makers: Heat and fan data would reveal exactly what is running on a device. The web gives only four rough levels, updated slowly. Apps use those to avoid pushing a laptop too hard.

use_cases.example: A video call app wanted real temperature to avoid overheating and uses the busy level.
A browser game wanted fan speed to lower graphics and uses frame rate drops as a hint.
A cloud gaming tab wanted heat readings and watches decoder stalls instead.
A browser editor wanted to throttle exports based on heat and reads the busy level.
A tracker wanted temperature as a device clue and cannot get it.
An IT portal wanted to monitor laptop health and needs a managed agent instead.
A browser hardware monitor site can show only coarse pressure, not true temperatures.

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
